title: introduce-state-silos-and-gpu-nodeclass-broker
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Private installs are increasingly hitting scale limits and operational friction when a single tfstate file, broad IAM roles, and undifferentiated GPU node pools are used across multiple tenants and AZ boundaries. This PR introduces two complementary Terraform modules and an orchestration helper to partition tfstate into "state silos" while providing a 'nodeclass-broker' that binds GPU nodeclass definitions, scoped IAM roles, and network attachment policies per tenant or workload class. Motivation: reduce blast radius for tfstate operations, enable smaller reconciliation units (faster applies), and support finer-grained IAM/egress controls for regulated workloads. What this PR does (high level): 1) new module terraform/modules/state-silo: implements a state partitioner pattern and remote state configuration helper that can be wired by tenant, region, or cluster-role. It includes lock/backup hooks and an opt-in 'drift-protector' workspace that snapshots resources before critical changes. 2) new module terraform/modules/nodeclass-broker: exposes a small Terraform interface to declare GPU nodeclasses (profile, taints/affinity, allowed instance types) and synthesizes tenant-scoped IAM roles, node pool labels, and subnet claim bindings. 3) small network templates terraform/modules/network-attachments to express per-nodeclass egress policies and cross-tenant VPC peering constraints. 4) a migration helper scripts/tfstate-partitioner/partitioner.go used offline to generate state mapping plans and run retries with exponential backoff; this is a declarative tool (not executed during apply) to aid operators. 5) updates to helm/values/private.yaml to expose nodeclass and state-silo settings that the installer consumes during chart render. 6) lightweight docs and examples in examples/tenant-silos/ that demonstrate a tenant-scoped rollout and rollback path. Migration story: a safe, staged migration is provided. The partitioner produces an ordered list of state moves, verifies resource counts post-move, and annotates the installer helm release with the new state-silo tag. There is a reversible path: every partition step also creates a 'shadow' tfstate snapshot in the configured artifacts bucket and a reconciler job that validates the new state before traffic cutover. Security: IAM roles generated by nodeclass-broker are intentionally narrow: they only grant kubelet-level permissions and specific KMS/encryption access for the tenant's nodeclass. We add KMS key policy examples and recommend using HSM-backed keys in the docs. Backwards compatibility: default behaviour is a single 'global' state silo and a single nodeclass to match existing installs; migration must be opt-in. Tests and CI: added unit tests for partitioner plan validation, Terraform fmt/validate checks, and end-to-end smoke run on a small test workspace in CI. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Private installs via a feature-flag gated helm/installer variable. Why different from prior work: instead of monolithic tfstate migrations or ad-hoc scripts, this PR formalizes a reusable module pattern, provides an operator tool to plan and verify moves, and couples nodeclass configuration to IAM and network policies so node lifecycle operations are lower risk. Related: ENG-4821 (state-silo initiative), ENG-4890 (gpu-nodeclass lifecycle).

review_comments:
Marco Ruiz (reviewer) commented on 2025-11-04: "Nice separation. Please clarify failure modes for partial state moves — what happens if snapshot creation succeeds but move fails?"
Asha Patel (author) replied on 2025-11-04: "Good question — the partitioner performs snapshot->plan->copy->verify sequence; if copy fails we retry with exponential backoff, and if repeated failures occur we leave a 'blocked' annotation and retain the shadow snapshot for rollback. Documented in README."
Zoe Lin requested changes on 2025-11-05: "IAM templates look permissive for service accounts we create — can we scope role names and resource ARNs to the tenant prefix and add least-privilege policy examples?"
Asha Patel replied on 2025-11-06: "Addressed: updated iam.tpl to interpolate tenant prefix and added an example policy for encrypted EBS and KMS use in the module README. Added tests to validate ARN patterns."
Daniel Ortega approved on 2025-11-09: "Approvals pending CI green — verified partition plan dry-run locally. Clean design."
release_notes: Introduce state-silos and nodeclass-broker Terraform modules for private installs. Operators can partition tfstate per-tenant/region, create tenant-scoped GPU nodeclasses with scoped IAM, and use the partitioner tool to plan safe migrations. Backwards compatible by default; migration opt-in. See examples/tenant-silos/README.md for migration steps.
notes_for_ops: Operators should stage migrations on non-production tenants first. Ensure artifacts bucket retention is at least 30 days for shadow snapshots. Feature flag helm.installer.stateSilos.enabled must be set to true to opt-in. Rolling back is supported by restoring shadow snapshots and re-annotating helm releases.
security_notes: IAM roles generated are tenant-scoped; recommend KMS HSM-backed keys. Audit logs are emitted during partition moves to the central audit bucket and should be monitored for repeated failures.
how_to_test: 1) terraform init + terraform plan in examples/tenant-silos/test-workspace (local backend) 2) run scripts/tfstate-partitioner/partitioner --dry-run to inspect proposed moves 3) enable helm.installer.stateSilos.enabled in a staging cluster and deploy the installer with nodeclass definitions 4) verify node pools are created with expected labels and IAM role binding 5) run partitioner plan and then apply steps against a disposable workspace to validate snapshot/verify flow.
